correctness.rationale: Stopped Brownian increment at rate r has centered Laplace density (c/2)exp(−c|x|), so reset epochs satisfy an affine perpetuity and exploration-time stationary position S_a=sum_{j>=0}a^j Z_j. The reset-state stationary law is aS_a. Markov-renewal occupation rewards weight active density by 1/r and resting density by tau0 e^{lambda|x|}; the conditional duration law matters through the mean only, with residual holding time needed for a Markov realization. Convolution with the leading Laplace increment and a contracted remainder having a strictly stronger exponential moment gives sharp f_a and g_a tails with positive coefficient c/(2P_a), c/(2aP_a), respectively. Integrability iff lambda<c/a follows at equality too; posterior odds are eta e^{lambda|x|}g_a/f_a, proving all three threshold cases. Its two-sided positive Laplace pole yields M_a(lambda)~c/[aP_a(c/a−lambda)] and active-fraction coefficient. Independent 45-digit mpmath partial-fraction tests confirmed f-tail at 3 x values and posterior asymptotics at 3 lambda values; these are supplementary finite tests.
risks: The conditional stationary assertion applies to augmented position/phase/residual duration, not an unconditioned transient ensemble.
At lambda≥c/a formal infinite measures may remain; only normalizable invariant probabilities are excluded.

value.rationale: A physically motivated reset-location-dependent recovery time creates a genuine separation between tail-level inferred phase inversion and loss of normalizable stationarity. The result fully classifies both thresholds, the nontrivial critical posterior, and a sharp occupation-collapse coefficient for a natural regenerative process.
risks: One-dimensional Brownian exploration, Poisson active clocks, fixed proportional contraction and conditional exponential mean dwell time. No universality for general holding laws, drift or nonlinear reset.

final_claim: For one-dimensional Brownian exploration with Poisson rate r, positional contraction a in (0,1) and refractory mean tau0 exp(lambda|reset_position|), a stationary physical-time probability exists exactly for lambda<c/a, c=sqrt(r/D). The distant-position resting posterior switches at lambda=c(1/a−1), with limiting values 0, eta/(a+eta), 1, and stationary active fraction vanishes linearly at c/a with prefactor a P_a/(eta c).
limitations: One-dimensional Brownian exploration, Poisson active clocks, fixed proportional contraction and conditional exponential mean dwell time. No universality for general holding laws, drift or nonlinear reset.
